dedupe_keys.name: evaluation of recent reports on the future of a net zero chemical industry in 2050 renewable carbon initiative 2024

description: This report compares 24 scenarios from 15 studies of how the chemical industry could reach net-zero emissions by 2050, focusing on the carbon feedstocks it would use. Across the scenarios, global feedstock demand grows 2.4-fold from 2020 to 2050, mostly outside Europe while European volumes stay stable, and the average net-zero mix is 22% biomass, 33% carbon capture and utilisation, 20% recycling and 24% fossil sources with carbon capture and storage, with recycling reaching 42% for plastics. It was written by Jörn Harrandt, Michael Carus and Christopher vom Berg of the nova-Institute as a scientific background report of the Renewable Carbon Initiative and published in November 2024. Coverage is global. The 20-page PDF is available to download free, with a DOI; no licence is stated. Caveats: it is a synthesis by an industry initiative that promotes renewable carbon, so the selection and averaging of scenarios reflect that aim, and it reports shares, not a scenario dataset. For simulation it gives consolidated pathways for chemical feedstocks, which help size future demand for biomass, captured CO2, recycling plants and hydrogen in energy and industrial infrastructure planning models. It is related to the Aspen Plant Scheduler and PAMSO records in this catalogue, which plan production in chemical plants.
